context:
Start with product shape, not implementation. The result explorer, hosted
API, and local artifact publishing should each have a separate contract and
success metric. Use the existing BenchBox export path as the anchor, then map
external reference patterns onto the repo's real deployment constraints.
description:
BenchBox currently blurs together three different concerns:
1) local/cloud artifact publication,
2) hosted result submission,
3) public result browsing and analysis on benchbox.dev.

That ambiguity makes the existing publishing TODO too large and too vague to
execute safely. This item defines the product boundary between those concerns,
chooses the initial site topology, and sequences the launch so BenchBox does
not jump directly from local result files to an open public submission portal.

The target output is a high-confidence strategy that distinguishes
`benchbox publish`, `benchbox submit`, and `benchbox.dev/results/`, plus a
delivery sequence the rest of the TODO cluster can depend on.

**Phase assignment:** This is a prerequisite planning item. Must complete before
any Phase 1 implementation begins. The refined strategy memo at
`_project/analysis/benchbox-results-platform-strategy.md` contains the current
recommended phasing: Phase 1 (static explorer MVP with repo-local
`results-data/`), Phase 2 (PR-based community contributions against that
corpus), Phase 3 (hosted API, only if demand warrants).

anti_patterns.dont: assume the static docs stack can absorb a rich results explorer unchanged
anti_patterns.why: interactive compare/search/auth workflows have different needs

anti_patterns.dont: collapse local artifact publication and hosted submission into one command surface
anti_patterns.why: the storage contract and service contract differ materially

preserves.behavior: The existing static GitHub Pages deployment for landing/docs/blog remains a valid baseline during planning
The schema-v2 result bundle remains the single canonical artifact for all downstream publishing and submission flows
